title: A heavier string
hook: Change linear mass density and predict wave speed.
misconception: wave speed doubles when linear mass density doubles, regardless of the stated relationship.
objective: Apply v = √(T/μ) to compare wave speed when linear mass density changes, under the stated assumptions.

claims.text: With a taut flexible string under fixed tension, v = √(T/μ). When linear mass density doubles, wave speed becomes 1/√2 times its original value.
claims.source: Idealized model v = √(T/μ); scaling exponent -0.5. Physics and assumptions await independent review.

recall.question: Consider a taut flexible string under fixed tension, with a nonzero initial result. If linear mass density triples from a positive value, what is the multiplier on wave speed?
recall.why: Apply v = √(T/μ) under the same assumptions: the multiplier is 1/√3.
